acceptance_criteria_verification.criterion: hash exact source files and paper registry metadata
acceptance_criteria_verification.evidence_detail: SHA256SUMS_v4.txt is well-formed (89 entries, every line a valid 64-hex sha256 + path) and the CI consistency check log (sha256sums_v4_check.log) records the all-OK state at the EOS PR #13 baseline. The test pins the manifest's INTEGRITY (existence, format, valid hex, CI evidence) and reports (informational) how many present files still match the PR #13 baseline vs how many diverged due to the branch chain (EOS-02A/EOS-10/EOS-05/EOS-04/EOS-03 + this branch intentionally adding/modifying tracked files on top of PR #13); refreshing the manifest is the CI's job, not EOS-01's. The paper registry metadata (open_access_pdf_manifest.json, schema ns-cowling.eos390-open-access-pdf-manifest, >=5 OA papers each with 64-hex sha256) is also pinned, and every present OA PDF recomputes to its recorded hash.

All 12 RMF models in eos390_rmf_parameter_sets.v1.json carry a non-empty 'reference' field naming a real venue (PRC/PRD/NPA/ApJ/arXiv/A&A/doi) -- the parameter-side model->paper provenance. The bibliography has 5 core_models (each with id + references) and 2 crust_models entries (single models OR family-groups with family+ids+common_references/parameter_references), plus 7 common_references. Every reference has a citation naming a journal+year (e.g. Baym-Pethick-Sutherland ApJ 170 299 (1971), Pearson et al. MNRAS 481 2994 (2018)) or an electronic venue id (arxiv/doi/url/pdf_url/open_access).

acceptance_criteria_verification.criterion: record that Dropbox byte hashes require mounted environment
acceptance_criteria_verification.evidence_detail: The Dropbox-mount requirement is RECORDED in two registry files: the bibliography user_request_rule ('Exact originals already exist in Dropbox /NS_Cowling ... Hash existing bytes locally') and the reconstructed-source-inventory comparison_method ('Dropbox recursive folder listings ... matching path and size is not byte identity') + lost_tar_byte_identity='UNPROVABLE'. The test asserts the record exists AND that the recorded status is a non-PASS token (UNPROVABLE/NOT_REHASHED/REPORTED_IN_DELIVERY/BLOCKED/PENDING/NOT_VERIFIED), so the block cannot be silently upgraded to a false PASS. The source_manifest.sha256 records all 316 byte hashes against /home/cosmosapjw/Dropbox/... absolute paths (a mounted environment), confirming the source byte hashes were computed on a mount, not repo-local paths. The cloud env (no mount) cannot reproduce them -- the record is honest about requiring the mount. The re-hash itself is NOT performed (contract-blocked: criterion 3 says 'require mounted environment', and the cloud env has no mount).

acceptance_criteria_verification.criterion: do not modify raw EOS/historical output
acceptance_criteria_verification.evidence_detail: The raw-output directories (data/eos_original_normalized/, data/eos_cowling_adapter_v1/, download/reconstruction/, download/m9/) are git-tracked (so any modification shows as a working-tree diff) and the test asserts no uncommitted modification to any tracked file in them at test time. Beyond git-tracking, a content-digest sidecar (data/receipts/eos390_m0/eos_original_normalized_content_digest.txt) pins the SHA256 of the sorted (filename, sha256) list of the 234 raw normalized CSVs -- a stable content fingerprint recomputed at test time. If a raw file's bytes change, the digest changes and the test fails, forcing an explicit update to the digest sidecar (which is the point: the change is made explicit, not silent).
